ce_bugs.text: Handler never validates booking.status, allowing guests to be added to cancelled/pending/rejected bookings and sending ICS files with status CONFIRMED that can resurrect cancelled events on calendars

Non-atomic write: prisma.booking.update persists attendees before updateCalendarAttendees; if the calendar update throws, a retry fails with a misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error, leaving the user unable to complete the calendar update
Unhandled findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId for unassigned round-robin bookings (userId: null coerced to 0) throws a raw Prisma RecordNotFound instead of a meaningful TRPCError
Seat-capacity bookings are bypassed: attendees are created with no seatsPerTimeSlot capacity check and without running seat logic, so full bookings can be overfilled
AddGuestsDialog's isInvalidEmail flag is never reset on success or when the user edits input, so reopening the dialog or fixing the input still shows a stale validation error
uniqueGuests silently filters out blacklisted and already-attending emails but still reports success, giving the organizer no feedback about guests who were not added
Organizer email subject uses attendees[0].name, which is empty for newly added guests, rendering a broken subject line instead of using the organizer entity

Guests array uniqueness is enforced only in the client component, not server-side, so direct API calls can create duplicate Attendee rows and duplicate emails (addGuests.schema.ts:5, addGuests.handler.ts:66-78)
Team permission check uses && instead of ||, so isTeamAdminOrOwner only passes for users who are both admin and owner, incorrectly denying team admins (addGuests.handler.ts:59-61)

Calendar update runs with the caller's credentials instead of the booking owner's, failing or mutating the organizer's calendar with the wrong identity when the caller is an attendee (addGuests.handler.ts:150-157)
No cap on guests array length and no rate limiting, allowing email amplification/spam abuse via attendee-initiated requests (addGuests.schema.ts:5, addGuests.handler.ts:106-116)
Case-sensitive comparison of guest vs existing attendee emails creates duplicate records and can select the wrong email template branch (addGuests.handler.ts:68-71)
Seat capacity (seatsPerTimeSlot) is not enforced when adding guests, silently overbooking seated events (addGuests.handler.ts:106-116)
Guests array schema has no length cap on the array or email strings, allowing unbounded DB inserts and email fan-out from a single authenticated request (any attendee can call the mutation)
isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...) check is likely wrong; should be || — team admins are denied access despite error paths suggesting otherwise
Blacklist comparison is case-mismatched (entries lowercased, guest not), allowing case-variant emails to bypass the blacklist and dedup check, causing duplicate attendee rows via createMany
EventManager is constructed with the requesting user's credentials (ctx.user) instead of the booking organizer's, so calendar attendee updates may run with wrong credentials

Authorization logic inverted: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&` instead of `||`, requiring both ADMIN and OWNER roles simultaneously, which are mutually exclusive, so team admins/owners cannot add guests to team bookings

Server input schema trusts client-side validation: no dedupe or case normalization of guest emails in the schema or handler, so API callers can insert duplicate attendee rows and trigger duplicate emails; validation schema is duplicated in the client component instead of reusing ZAddGuestsInputSchema

EventManager is constructed with the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's: when the caller is an attendee or a non-owner team admin, the calendar-attendee update runs with wrong credentials while DB writes and emails still succeed, causing DB/email/calendar divergence
No seat-capacity enforcement for seated event types: the handler reads seatsPerTimeSlot but never checks it before createMany, allowing attendee count to exceed the advertised seat limit
Organizer lookup uses findFirstOrThrow with `booking.userId || 0`, which throws an unhandled raw Prisma P2025 error (500) instead of a typed TRPCError when booking.userId is null

Calendar update (updateCalendarAttendees) is called after the DB write without a transaction or try/catch, so a calendar failure leaves guests committed to DB while retries are blocked because uniqueGuests length becomes 0 and throws BAD_REQUEST — no retry, compensation, or user recovery path exists
Authorization check uses && instead of || when combining isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, meaning only users who are both admin AND owner pass, locking out team admins with FORBIDDEN

Blacklist comparison is case-asymmetric: blacklisted emails are lowercased but incoming guest values are compared raw, allowing 'Spam@Example.com' to bypass a blacklist entry of 'spam@example.com'; attendee-dedup check has the same case-sensitivity issue causing duplicate attendees and emails

EventManager is built from the calling user's (ctx.user) credentials instead of the booking organizer's, so calendar attendee updates run with the wrong user's calendar credentials — failing or mutating the wrong calendar when non-organizers add guests

prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow with where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } throws an unhandled Prisma error surfaced as a generic 500 for bookings with null userId instead of a meaningful NOT_FOUND/BAD_REQUEST

isInvalidEmail error state in AddGuestsDialog is set true on failed validation but only reset via Cancel, so after a successful retry the 'Emails must be unique and valid' warning remains rendered alongside the success toast
Authorization check uses `&&` instead of `||` when verifying isTeamAdminOrOwner, locking team admins out of managing guests; variable name is misleading either way

Email uniqueness validation exists only in client-side inline schema; server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema allows duplicate emails within a single request, creating duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails
Blacklist filtering and attendee dedupe are case-sensitive: guest emails are not lowercased before comparison, allowing case variants to bypass blacklist and create duplicate attendees
EventManager is built from the acting caller's credentials instead of the booking owner's, so calendar attendee updates fail or are skipped when a non-owner adds guests
Email send failures are silently swallowed with console.log only, discarding the error object with no telemetry or error tracking
isInvalidEmail state in AddGuestsDialog is never reset on successful add or on value change, causing a stale validation warning to appear when the dialog is reopened
Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||, so team admins who are not owners are denied even though the UI allows them to manage guests
Partial failure: attendees are persisted to DB before calendar update, which is unguarded; if it throws, guests remain in DB and retry produces misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error
Calendar update uses the actor's credentials instead of the organizer's/booking owner's, so attendee-triggered guest additions may fail or silently not update the calendar event
No booking status check: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings and receive CONFIRMED ICS invites for meetings that no longer exist
Server schema omits uniqueness rule; duplicate emails within one request create duplicate attendee rows since dedupe only filters against existing attendees
Blacklisted guest emails are silently dropped while the API reports success, or triggers confusing 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error when all emails are blacklisted
Email send failures are fully swallowed (console log only) and the dialog always shows success toast, so users believe emails were sent even when all failed
Any attendee can add unlimited guests (no cap on guests array), enabling phishing/mail-bombing via emails impersonating the organizer with organizer's from/replyTo
Stale validation error in AddGuestsDialog: isInvalidEmail is set on failure but never cleared, so the error banner persists even after correction

mrv_findings.text: renderEmail("AttendeeAddGuestsEmail", ...) and renderEmail("OrganizerAddGuestsEmail", ...) reference template names never registered in the renderer (packages/emails/src/index.ts), so every Add-Guests email send throws an unknown-template error or returns html: undefined — or fails the TypeScript build if the selector is a typed union (P1)

t("additional_guests") in BookingListItem.tsx:196 and AddGuestsDialog.tsx:60 relies on a locale key not added in the diff's common.json changes, causing the 'Additional guests' menu item and dialog header to render the raw key (or empty string) in every locale including en (P2)
No tests added for any of the new server-side logic in addGuests.handler.ts, including the permission matrix, uniqueGuests filter, sendAddGuestsEmails routing, and new email templates
addGuests.handler.ts:51-53 — isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, so team admins who are not owners are incorrectly forbidden from adding guests
addGuests.handler.ts:31-38 — no check on booking.status, allowing guests to be added to cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings, which sends CONFIRMED ics attachments for nonexistent events

addGuests.handler.ts:66-74 — blacklist check and attendee dedupe are case-sensitive while blacklist is lowercased, allowing bypass via case variation (e.g. Spam@x.com bypasses spam@x.com block) and duplicate attendees

addGuests.handler.ts:160-165 — seat-based event types only copy seat metadata for emails; no capacity check or seat-booking association, allowing overbooking beyond seatsPerTimeSlot and potential email leakage when seatsShowAttendees is false
addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests array has no .max() limit, enabling unbounded attendees and an email-bomb/DoS vector against mail and calendar providers
addGuests.handler.ts:167-170 — email send failure is swallowed with only a console.log and reported as success, so guests may never be notified while the user sees a success toast
Authorization check uses && instead of || in isTeamAdminOrOwner, requiring BOTH admin AND owner roles so team admins are silently locked out of guest management on team bookings
No server-side uniqueness enforcement for duplicates within the input array; duplicate emails in the guests input create duplicate attendee rows and cause duplicate emails and ICS REQUESTs to be sent
Case-sensitive email comparison: blacklist entries are lowercased but incoming guest emails are not, allowing blacklist bypass via casing and defeating the duplicate attendee check
No booking.status invariant check, allowing guests to be added to cancelled or rejected bookings, after which ICS REQUEST/CONFIRMED updates resurrect the cancelled event in attendees' calendars
Seated event types are handled but seat capacity is never checked against seatsPerTimeSlot and no BookingSeat records are created for new attendees, allowing overbooking and inconsistent seat data
isAttendee grants write access for any attendee to add arbitrary guests and send emails as the organizer, an email amplification vector beyond the stated organizer-guest-management scope

EventManager is built with the requesting user's credentials rather than the booking owner's, so for non-organizer callers the calendar update targets the wrong account, and it throws after the DB write without try/catch leaving the mutation half-applied
AddGuestsDialog's isInvalidEmail state is never reset on the success path, causing a stale error banner to display the next time the dialog opens
The isTeamAdminOrOwner check requires the caller to be BOTH admin AND owner instead of either, denying legitimate team admins with FORBIDDEN
Admin/owner check consults booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0 instead of booking.teamId, so team bookings with deleted event types become unmanageable except by the original organizer
Server does not enforce guest uniqueness within the guests array; the invariant lives only in a client-side zod schema, allowing direct API callers to create duplicate attendee rows
Blacklist check is case-sensitive: blacklist entries are lowercased but the guest email is not, making the blacklist bypassable by case variation
Unbounded guests array with no max(), rate limit, or attendee cap lets any attendee mail-bomb the organizer, team, and prior guests in repeated calls
Check-then-insert against stale data with no transaction or UNIQUE(bookingId, email) constraint causes duplicate attendees under concurrent requests

Non-atomic write-then-side-effect sequence: if the calendar update throws after attendees are persisted, a retry is rejected with BAD_REQUEST, permanently wedging the user; swallowed email errors also report success when nothing was sent
EventManager is constructed from the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, so calendar attendee sync fails for attendee or team admin callers
No booking status guard: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/pending bookings, re-sending CONFIRMED ICS invites that resurrect cancelled events on attendees' calendars
newGuests.includes(attendee.email) decides email template by case-sensitive string match rather than an explicit 'is new' flag, breaking silently if any email normalization is introduced upstream

Authorization logic in addGuests.handler.ts:57-58 uses && instead of || between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, silently narrowing permission to admin AND owner and locking team admins (non-owners) out of the addGuests feature

isAttendee escape hatch in addGuests.handler.ts:53-62 allows any attendee to inject unlimited guests with no .max() on the array, enabling free calendar REQUEST emails to arbitrary addresses with no UI or design justification in the diff

In addGuests.handler.ts:144-150, when caller is an attendee, EventManager is built from ctx.user credentials but evt.destinationCalendar belongs to the organizer, causing silent calendar sync failure while DB/email succeed; errors in updateCalendarAttendees are not caught

No booking.status check in addGuests.handler.ts or email templates; cancelled/rejected bookings can mint CONFIRMED ics invites with status hardcoded to CONFIRMED and method REQUEST, re-confirming dead events

Blacklist comparison in addGuests.handler.ts:73-77 is case-asymmetric: blacklist emails are lowercased but the candidate guest is used raw, so differently-cased blacklisted addresses bypass the filter; same block also case-mismatches attendee dedupe causing duplicate attendee rows

sendAddGuestsEmails in email-manager.ts:545 receives raw input guests instead of the persisted uniqueGuests, so pre-existing or blacklisted attendee emails matching attendee addresses receive full AttendeeScheduledEmail confirmations instead of the 'new guests added' notice

AddGuestsDialog.tsx:23-27 forks the validation schema client-side instead of importing the shared server ZAddGuestsInputSchema; client enforces uniqueness via refine while server does not, so client and server accept different inputs

Booking lookup in addGuests.handler.ts has no user/org scope and the post-fetch check grants write access to mere attendees, letting any attendee of any booking inject arbitrary new attendees via addGuests
Emails sent with replyTo set to the organizer's email can target attacker-chosen addresses, creating an email-sending/spam/phishing vector with no rate limit
updateCalendarAttendees allows a non-owner attendee to mutate the organizer's calendar event attendee list
NOT_FOUND-vs-FORBIDDEN response split allows probing which booking IDs exist

BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS check is bypassed by case variation: blacklist entries are lowercased but the guest string compared is never lowercased, so blacklisted emails with uppercase characters are accepted

Email uniqueness is enforced only client-side: the server schema has no uniqueness refinement and uniqueGuests only dedupes against existing attendees, so duplicate emails in a single request create duplicate attendee rows, corrupt the ICS/attendee list, and send duplicate emails

updateCalendarAttendees runs with the requesting user's credentials instead of the booking owner's, causing silent failures (inconsistent DB/email vs calendar state) or an attacker-controlled write path in the attendee case
isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && where || is required, so team admins (non-owners) fail the check and only owners satisfy it, deviating from the intended authorization matrix
booking.eventType can be null (left-joined), causing the admin/owner check to silently evaluate against teamId 0

Attendee rows are written to the DB before the calendar update, with no transaction and no rollback: if the calendar provider errors, guest rows persist in the DB while the calendar event and emails are never updated, leaving half-migrated state that cannot be rolled back through the application

Dedup check uses exact-case string equality (guest === attendee.email) with no lowercasing, so a differently-cased duplicate email permanently creates a duplicate attendee row that is emailed and added to the calendar twice, with no removal path

Email-send failure is swallowed with only a console.log, so the handler returns 'Guests added' and the DB write succeeds while no guests or organizer are notified and no ICS REQUEST update is delivered, with no way to re-trigger the emails
